##: The manifest published to the Scoop bucket, where it lives as bucket/shep.json.
This copy is the source of truth; the `scoop` job in
.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml stamps the version, url and hash and
pushes the result on each release.
NOT INSTALLABLE AS COMMITTED. The version below is 0.0.0 and the hash is a
sentinel, so this copy names an archive no release carries. The push job fails
loudly if either sentinel survives substitution.
checkver and autoupdate are here so the bucket can bump itself if it ever runs
Scoop's excavator workflow. They are not what the release job uses. The hash
url ends .sha256 on the archive's BASE name, not on its full filename: the
sidecar is shep-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.sha256, and $url.sha256 would have
asked for a .zip.sha256 that does not exist.
One architecture. shep publishes x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and nothing else on
Windows: no 32-bit build, and no arm64 one yet.
No extract_dir. The release archives put the binaries at the archive root
rather than under a version-named directory.
bin lists shep.exe only. shep-runtime and shep-dev are container entrypoint
aliases with no desktop use case, the same call the Chocolatey package makes.
description: Process manager that keeps a flock of long-running processes alive, with logs, watch and cron restarts, and webhook alerts
notes: shep startup is not built on Windows: boot-time supervision there needs a
Service Control Manager service. Run shep start in your own session, or wrap
shep runtime in NSSM or WinSW.
shep stop has no SIGTERM equivalent to send, so it waits out the app's whole
kill_timeout unless the app opts into the shepherd channel.
The user and group Flockfile fields refuse permanently on Windows.
